note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council, 1936. Nominations were lodged on 5 May; 'There are no contests for the County Council. The 27 electoral areas will be represented in the new Council by 16 Unionists and 11 Nationalists' (Ulster Herald, 9 May 1936, p. 5), and the Belfast News-Letter of 6 May 1936, p. 9 names the only changes in personnel: Coagh, Donaghmore, Killeter, Pomeroy and Trillick; no nomination was received for Dromore, whose member was deemed re-elected. The unchanged divisions are recorded by the meeting method (7 Nov 2026): each member is the 1933 return for the division (Mid-Ulster Mail, 22 April 1933, p. 6), or, for Ballygawley and Newtownstewart, the member co-opted in 1934 after a death, and each sat on the new council in 1936 (first meeting of Monday 15 June 1936, Ulster Herald, 20 June 1936, p. 3; later meetings of August and September 1936). Omagh Urban's outgoing member, Mr. A. E. Donnelly, M.P., co-opted in May 1935 on the death of Mr. Michael Lynch (Ulster Herald, 1 June 1935, p. 10), was selected as the Nationalist county council candidate on 3 May 1936 (Belfast News-Letter, 4 May 1936, p. 9) and returned unopposed. The polling day for Tyrone was Wednesday 3 June 1936; there was no county council contest. Filed on 1936-06-03, the Tyrone polling day (previously filed under 1936-05-28, 6 Nov 2026). The sitting member, co-opted in May 1935 in room of the late Michael Lynch (Ulster Herald, 1 June 1935, p. 10). The selection report prints no label for the county seat; he was the Nationalists' choice. Returned unopposed.
